title: Daily Devotional #21
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #21
Dear Lord,

As I read through Matthew chapter 21 today, I am struck by the many different reactions to your presence and your teachings. Some people praised you and welcomed you as the Son of David, while others rejected you and sought to kill you.
It's easy to focus on the negative reactions and wonder why people would reject you, but I want to instead focus on the positive reactions and praise you for who you are.

In verse 9, we read that the crowds who went ahead of you and those who followed shouted, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" They recognized you as the long-awaited Messiah, the one who would save them from their sins and restore their nation. And as they laid their cloaks and palm branches on the ground for you to ride over, they demonstrated their willingness to follow you and submit to your authority.

Lord, I want to have that same heart of praise and submission. I want to recognize you as my Savior and King, and willingly lay down my life for you. Help me to remember that you are not just a great teacher or moral example, but you are the Son of God who came to save me and all of humanity.

In verse 12, we read that you entered the temple and drove out all who were buying and selling there, and overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves. You were angry because they had turned your Father's house into a den of robbers.

Lord, help me to be passionate about the things that matter to you. Help me to have a zeal for your kingdom and to stand up against anything that would defile or diminish it. And help me to remember that my body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, and to treat it with the same reverence and respect that you showed for your Father's house.
In verse 21, we read that you cursed a fig tree that had no fruit on it, and it withered away. This was a symbol of the judgment that would come upon those who did not bear fruit in their lives.

Lord, I don't want to be like that fig tree. I want to bear fruit for your kingdom and to make a difference in the world. Help me to be a faithful and fruitful disciple, and to use the gifts and talents you have given me to bring glory to your name.
In closing, I want to echo the words of the crowds in verse 9 and say, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" You are my Savior and King, and I praise you for who you are and all that you have done for me.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #22
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #22
Dear God,

Today I read Matthew chapter 22 and was struck by the profound message that You have for me in this chapter. The chapter opens with the parable of the wedding banquet, where the king invites people to come and join him in the celebration of his son's marriage. However, those who were initially invited refused to come, and instead, the king sent his servants to invite anyone they could find, good or bad, to fill the banquet hall. This parable reminds me of Your great love for us and Your desire for us to join You in Your kingdom. It also reminds me of the importance of accepting Your invitation and not turning away from it.

Later in the chapter, the Pharisees try to trap Jesus by asking Him which commandment is the greatest. Jesus responds by saying that the greatest commandment is to love God with all your heart, soul, and mind, and the second is to love your neighbor as yourself. This reminds me that all of Your commandments are based on love, and if I am truly following You, then I will love others as You have loved me.

In the same conversation, Jesus asks the Pharisees about the identity of the Messiah, and they answer that He is the son of David. Jesus then quotes from Psalm 110, where David calls the Messiah his Lord, indicating that the Messiah is more than just a son of David, but is also divine. This reminds me of Your incredible plan for salvation and how Jesus, as both fully human and fully divine, is the perfect sacrifice for our sins.

Finally, in the last section of the chapter, Jesus asks the Pharisees about the identity of the Messiah's son. They answer that he is the heir to the kingdom. Jesus then quotes from Psalm 118, where the rejected stone becomes the cornerstone, indicating that the Messiah's son is not only the heir to the kingdom but also the foundation of it. This reminds me that even though we may feel rejected or insignificant, You have a plan for us, and we can trust that You will use us to build Your kingdom in ways that we may not even imagine.
Thank You for this reminder of Your love and plan for our lives. Help me to accept Your invitation to Your kingdom, to love others as You have loved me, and to trust in Your plan for my life. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #9
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #9
Dear God,

As I read through Matthew chapter 9, I am struck by the power and compassion of Jesus. He healed the sick, forgave sins, and called sinners to repentance. He showed us what it truly means to be a servant of God, by reaching out to those in need and demonstrating your love in practical ways.

In verses 2-7, we see how Jesus heals a paralyzed man. He not only healed the man physically, but also forgave his sins. This reminds me that you are not only concerned with our physical well-being, but also our spiritual well-being. You desire to forgive us of our sins and make us whole.

In verses 9-13, we see how Jesus calls Matthew, a tax collector, to follow him. Jesus did not come for the righteous, but for sinners. This is a reminder that no matter how far we have strayed from you, you are always willing to accept us back into your loving arms. Your grace is sufficient for us, and you are always willing to forgive us when we come to you with a contrite heart.

In verses 18-26, we see how Jesus heals a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years, and raises a young girl from the dead. These miracles show us that nothing is impossible for you. You have the power to heal us physically, emotionally, and spiritually. We need only to come to you in faith, trusting in your goodness and mercy.

Finally, in verses 35-38, we see how Jesus had compassion on the crowds, who were like sheep without a shepherd. He encouraged his disciples to pray for more workers to go out into the harvest field. This is a reminder that we are called to be your hands and feet in this world, to bring hope and healing to those who are hurting. We need to pray for more workers to join us in this mission, and to be willing to step out in faith and serve wherever you call us.

Lord, thank you for the example of Jesus in Matthew chapter 9. Help us to follow his example of compassion and service, and to trust in your power and goodness. May we be your ambassadors in this world, bringing hope and healing to those who are in need. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #37
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #37
Dear Heavenly Father,

Today, I spent time reading and meditating on Mark 9, and I am grateful for the wisdom and guidance that I have gained from it. The chapter begins with the story of the Transfiguration, where Jesus reveals His divine nature to Peter, James, and John. As I read this story, I am reminded of Your power and glory, and I am filled with a sense of awe and wonder.

But as I continue reading, I am also confronted with the harsh reality of the world we live in. The disciples encounter a boy possessed by an evil spirit, and despite their efforts, they are unable to drive it out. It is only when Jesus intervenes that the boy is finally freed from the demon's grasp. This story reminds me that there are forces at work in this world that are beyond our human ability to overcome, but with faith and trust in You, all things are possible.

In this chapter, Jesus also teaches His disciples about the importance of humility and service. He tells them that whoever wants to be first must be last and servant of all. As I reflect on this teaching, I am reminded that as a follower of Christ, my life should be characterized by humility and a willingness to serve others.

Finally, in Mark 9, Jesus warns His disciples about the dangers of sin and the need for radical obedience. He says that if our hands or feet cause us to sin, we should cut them off, and if our eyes cause us to sin, we should pluck them out. While this may seem like a harsh teaching, it is a reminder that sin is a serious matter, and we must be willing to take drastic measures to avoid it.

As I close this devotional journal, I pray that the lessons I have learned from Mark 9 will stay with me and guide me in my walk with You. I pray that I will always remember Your power and glory, the reality of the spiritual battles we face, the importance of humility and service, and the need for radical obedience in the face of sin. Thank You for Your love and grace, and for the wisdom and guidance You provide through Your Word.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #11
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #11
Dear Lord,
As I read through Matthew chapter 11, I am struck by the powerful words of Jesus and the depth of His love and compassion for His people.

First, I am reminded of John the Baptist, who sent his disciples to ask Jesus if He was the Messiah. Jesus responds by pointing to the miracles He has performed and the fulfillment of prophecy in His ministry. But then He goes on to say something truly remarkable: "Blessed is anyone who does not stumble on account of me." (Matthew 11:6) Even when people question His identity or doubt His message, Jesus continues to extend grace and offer hope.

Next, Jesus turns His attention to the towns where He has performed miracles but has not been received with faith. He says, "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes." (Matthew 11:21) This is a sobering reminder of the importance of recognizing and responding to the work of God in our midst.

But perhaps the most comforting and reassuring words in this chapter come from Jesus Himself: "Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy and my burden is light." (Matthew 11:28-30) How often do we carry the weight of our worries and fears, feeling like we are all alone in our struggles? But Jesus invites us to come to Him, to take on His yoke and find rest for our souls. He is gentle and humble, and His burden is light.

Lord, I pray that I would take these words to heart and live in the light of Your grace and compassion. May I recognize Your work in my life and respond with faith and obedience. And when I am weary and burdened, may I come to You and find rest for my soul. In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #13
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #13
Dear God,

As I read through Matthew chapter 13, I am struck by the depth and complexity of the parables that Jesus used to teach the crowds. Each story carries a powerful message that speaks to the human heart in a unique way, and I am reminded of the importance of listening closely to your word and allowing it to take root in my life.

The parable of the sower, in particular, speaks to me deeply. I am reminded that your word is like seed, and that the way I receive it can make all the difference in how it grows and bears fruit. If I am like the rocky soil, receiving your word with enthusiasm but quickly losing heart when challenges arise, I will never truly understand its power. But if I am like the good soil, receiving your word with an open heart and a willingness to be transformed, then I can be a part of your kingdom work in the world.

I am also challenged by the parable of the weeds. It is so easy to judge others and try to root out what we perceive as evil in the world, but Jesus reminds us that it is not our job to do so. Only you, Lord, have the power to judge, and it is our job to focus on our own growth and transformation in you. Help me to trust in your justice and to cultivate a heart of love and compassion for all people.

Finally, I am encouraged by the parables of the mustard seed and the yeast. They remind me that your kingdom work may start small, but it has the power to grow and transform the world in ways we could never imagine. Help me to trust in your power and to be faithful in the small things, knowing that you are working all things together for good.
Thank you, Lord, for your word and for the ways it speaks to our hearts. Help me to be a faithful listener and a faithful follower, always seeking to grow in my love for you and for others.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #26
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #26
Dear God,

As I read Matthew chapter 26, I am struck by the depth of emotions that Jesus experienced in the hours leading up to His arrest, trial, and crucifixion. The chapter opens with Jesus telling His disciples that the Passover meal they are about to share together will be His last before His death. He knows what lies ahead, yet He continues to love and serve His disciples to the very end.

As I reflect on Jesus' example, I am reminded of the importance of sacrificial love. Jesus' love for His disciples was so great that He willingly gave up His own life for them. I am called to love others in the same way, to put their needs above my own and to serve them with humility and grace.

But as the chapter progresses, Jesus' emotions begin to shift. He goes to the Garden of Gethsemane to pray, and there He expresses his anguish to His Father. He says, "My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow to the point of death" (Matthew 26:38). Even though Jesus knows what is going to happen and is willing to face it, He is not immune to the pain and fear that come with such a great sacrifice.

Lord, as I face difficult situations in my life, help me to remember that it is okay to feel overwhelmed and afraid. Even Jesus, who was fully God and fully human, experienced these emotions. Help me to turn to You in prayer and to seek Your comfort and strength.

Finally, in Matthew 26, we see Jesus' ultimate act of obedience to His Father. He willingly submits to His arrest and trial, knowing that it will lead to His death on the cross. He does not resist or fight back, but instead He surrenders Himself to God's plan.

Lord, help me to follow Jesus' example of obedience. Give me the courage to trust in Your plan for my life, even when it is difficult or painful. Help me to surrender my will to Yours and to walk in faith and obedience, just as Jesus did.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #31
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #31
Dear Heavenly Father,

As I read through Mark chapter 3, I am reminded of the importance of prioritizing my relationship with You above all else. In this chapter, Jesus prioritizes spending time with His disciples, healing the sick, and ministering to the crowds over His own physical needs and desires.

One of the things that stands out to me in this chapter is how the Pharisees and religious leaders are constantly questioning and challenging Jesus' actions. Yet, Jesus remains steadfast in His mission to do the will of His Father and to bring healing and salvation to those who need it.

Lord, I pray that I would have the same level of determination and commitment to follow Your will for my life, even when others question or oppose me. I pray that You would give me the strength and wisdom to discern Your will and to pursue it with all my heart, soul, and mind.

As I continue to read through Mark chapter 3, I am struck by the power of Jesus' healing ministry. The sick and the demon-possessed come to Him, and He heals them all. It is a powerful reminder that You are a God who cares deeply about our physical and emotional well-being.

Lord, I pray that You would bring healing to those who are sick, struggling, or hurting in any way. I pray that You would work in miraculous ways to bring wholeness and restoration to their lives, just as You did in the lives of those who came to Jesus for healing.

Finally, I am reminded of the importance of community and fellowship. In this chapter, Jesus calls His disciples to be with Him, and they begin to form a close-knit community that supports and encourages one another.

Lord, I pray that You would help me to prioritize my relationships with other believers, and that You would help me to be a source of encouragement and support to those around me. I pray that You would use me to build up Your church and to bring glory to Your name.
In Jesus' name, I pray. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #18
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #18
Dear God,

As I read through Matthew chapter 18 today, I am struck by the theme of humility and forgiveness that runs throughout the chapter. It is a reminder that in order to follow you, we must be willing to put aside our pride and seek reconciliation with others.

In the beginning of the chapter, Jesus teaches us about the importance of humility. He tells us that we must become like little children in order to enter the kingdom of heaven. This means that we must approach you with a childlike faith, without any preconceived notions or biases. We must be willing to learn from you and submit ourselves to your will.

Later in the chapter, Jesus speaks about forgiveness. He tells us that if someone sins against us, we should first try to resolve the issue between us alone. But if they refuse to listen, we should bring one or two others with us to try to help them see the error of their ways. And if they still refuse to listen, we should bring it to the church. Ultimately, if the person still refuses to repent, we should treat them as an outsider.

However, even in this scenario, Jesus tells us to forgive. He says that if someone sins against us and repents, we should forgive them seventy times seven. This is not an easy thing to do, but it is necessary if we want to live in peace with one another and with you.

Lord, as I reflect on these teachings, I am convicted of my own pride and unwillingness to forgive at times. Please help me to become more humble and to seek reconciliation with others, even when it is difficult. And help me to remember that forgiveness is not just a commandment, but a gift that you have given to us through your sacrifice on the cross.
Thank you for your love and grace, and for the wisdom that you impart to us through your Word. May I continue to grow in my faith and become more like you each day.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #10
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #10
Dear God,

Today, I spent some time reading Matthew chapter 10, and it really spoke to me. The chapter is all about your call to your disciples to go out and preach the gospel, heal the sick, and drive out demons. As I read, I was struck by how much trust and faith you placed in your disciples to carry out this important work.

One verse that particularly stood out to me was Matthew 10:16, where you say, "I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves." This verse reminds me that as your follower, I must always be prepared to face adversity and opposition. But at the same time, I must also maintain my purity and innocence in the face of temptation and sin.

I also love how you encourage your disciples to not worry about what they will say when they are brought before authorities. You tell them that the Holy Spirit will give them the words to say. This is such a powerful reminder that I too should rely on the Holy Spirit to guide my words and actions, especially when I am in difficult or challenging situations.

Finally, I was struck by the urgency of your message in this chapter. You tell your disciples to go out and preach, heal, and drive out demons because the harvest is plentiful but the workers are few. This is a reminder that there are still so many people in the world who need to hear the good news of your love and salvation. It's up to us, your followers, to share that message with the world.

As I go about my day today, I pray that I will be like your disciples in Matthew 10 - faithful, obedient, and bold in sharing your message with others. Help me to rely on the Holy Spirit for wisdom and guidance, and to never lose sight of the urgency of this task. Thank you for your love and grace, and for the privilege of being called to serve you.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #25
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #25
Dear God,

As I read through Matthew Chapter 25 today, I was struck by the powerful message of stewardship and service that is present throughout the chapter. From the parable of the ten virgins to the story of the talents, there is a consistent message that we are to be good stewards of the gifts and resources that You have given us.

The first story about the ten virgins highlights the importance of being prepared for Your return. The wise virgins were prepared with oil for their lamps, while the foolish ones were not. This parable reminds me that I need to be diligent in my preparation for Your return, so that I am ready to meet You when the time comes.

The second story about the talents emphasizes the importance of using our gifts and resources wisely. The servant who buried his talent was rebuked, while the ones who invested their talents were rewarded. This parable challenges me to consider how I am using the resources that You have given me to serve Your kingdom.

Lord, as I reflect on these parables, I am reminded that You have entrusted me with many gifts and resources, and that I am called to be a faithful steward of them. Help me to be wise and diligent in my preparation for Your return, and to use my gifts and resources to serve Your kingdom in the most effective way possible.

I pray that You would give me the wisdom and discernment that I need to use my gifts and resources in a way that is pleasing to You. I ask that You would use me to be a blessing to others, and that You would help me to be faithful in all that You have called me to do.

Thank You for Your grace and mercy, and for the many blessings that You have given me. May Your name be glorified through my life, and may I be a faithful servant who hears Your words, "Well done, good and faithful servant!" when You return.
In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #17
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #17
Dear God,

As I reflect on Matthew chapter 17, I am reminded of the power and glory of Your Son, Jesus Christ. In this chapter, Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain where He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun and His clothes became as white as the light. Then, Moses and Elijah appeared and spoke with Him.

This event must have been truly awe-inspiring for the disciples. They were witnesses to Jesus’ divine nature and His connection to the great prophets of the past. As I read this story, I am reminded of the importance of recognizing Jesus as more than just a human being. He is the Son of God, and His divinity sets Him apart from all other people who have ever lived.

Lord, I pray that I never lose sight of the magnitude of who Jesus is. Help me to remember that He is not just a great teacher or a moral leader, but He is the Savior of the world. Help me to worship Him with reverence and awe, knowing that He is worthy of all honor and glory.

In this chapter, we also see Jesus healing a boy who was possessed by a demon. The disciples had been unable to cast out the demon, but Jesus rebuked the demon and it left the boy. This miracle shows that there is no limit to Jesus’ power and that He is able to do anything that is according to Your will, God.

Lord, I pray that You would increase my faith in Your power and in Your ability to work miracles in my life. Help me to trust You in all circumstances and to have confidence that You are working all things together for my good.
Thank You, Lord, for the truths that are contained in Matthew chapter 17. Help me to apply them to my life and to live in a way that honors and glorifies Your Son, Jesus Christ.
In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #32
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #32
Dear God,

As I read through Mark 4, I am struck by the parables that Jesus told. These stories may have seemed simple on the surface, but they contained deep spiritual truths that required careful reflection and meditation to fully understand.

The first parable, the parable of the sower, teaches us about the different ways in which people respond to your message. Some people hear your word but do not understand it, while others receive it with joy but quickly fall away when faced with persecution or difficulty. Still, others hear your word, understand it, and bear fruit in their lives. Lord, I pray that I would be like the good soil, receiving your word and allowing it to take root in my heart and produce a bountiful harvest of righteousness.

The second parable, the parable of the mustard seed, shows us that your kingdom may start small, but it will grow and expand until it fills the whole earth. Lord, I pray that I would be faithful in planting seeds of your word wherever I go, knowing that even the smallest act of kindness or word of encouragement can have a tremendous impact when done in your name.

The third parable, the parable of the lamp, reminds us that your truth should be proclaimed openly and not hidden away. Lord, I pray that I would be bold in sharing your truth with others, even when it is unpopular or uncomfortable.

Finally, the fourth parable, the parable of the storm, shows us that even when we face the storms of life, you are always with us and will calm the winds and waves with your word. Lord, I pray that I would have faith in you during the storms of life, knowing that you are always in control and will never leave me or forsake me.
Thank you for the lessons you teach us through your word. Help me to apply these truths to my life and to live a life that honors you.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #27
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #27
Dear God,

As I read through Matthew chapter 27, I am overwhelmed with emotions. This chapter recounts the betrayal, trial, crucifixion, and burial of your son, Jesus Christ. It is one of the most painful and heartbreaking moments in human history.

The chapter starts with the betrayal of Jesus by Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples. Judas betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, which was the price of a slave. It is hard to imagine how someone who walked so closely with Jesus could betray him for such a small amount of money.

Then, Jesus is brought before the high priest and the Sanhedrin for trial. The religious leaders accuse him of blasphemy and seek to put him to death. Despite the false accusations and the mockery, Jesus remained silent, knowing that his mission was to die for the sins of humanity.

The chapter goes on to describe the brutal crucifixion of Jesus. He was mocked, beaten, and nailed to a cross. He endured excruciating pain and suffering for hours before finally giving up his spirit and dying. It is hard to fathom the depth of love that Jesus had for us to endure such agony.

Lastly, we read about the burial of Jesus. Joseph of Arimathea, a member of the Sanhedrin, took Jesus' body and placed it in his own tomb. This fulfilled the prophecy that Jesus would be buried with the rich.

As I reflect on this chapter, I am reminded of the immense sacrifice that Jesus made for us. He willingly gave up his life so that we could be reconciled to you, God. He suffered so that we could have eternal life. This chapter is a reminder of the price that was paid for our salvation.
Lord, I pray that I never take for granted the sacrifice that was made for me. Help me to live a life that honors you and the gift of salvation that you have given us through Jesus Christ.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #12
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #12
Dear God,
As I read through Matthew chapter 12, I am struck by the ways in which Jesus challenges the religious leaders of his time and invites his followers to deepen their faith and commitment to him.

One of the most powerful moments in this chapter is when Jesus heals a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath. The Pharisees are outraged by this, as they believe it is against the law to perform any work on the Sabbath. But Jesus reminds them that it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath, and that compassion and mercy are at the heart of God's law.

This passage reminds me that sometimes we can get so caught up in rules and regulations that we forget about the most important thing - love. Jesus shows us that love and mercy are at the center of God's will for our lives, and that sometimes we need to break the rules in order to show that love to others.

Another important lesson from this chapter is the importance of bearing good fruit. Jesus tells us that a tree is known by its fruit, and that a good tree will produce good fruit. This reminds me that it is not enough to simply say that we believe in you, Lord - we must also live out that faith in our actions and our words.

As I reflect on this chapter, I am reminded of the incredible love and compassion that you have for us, God. You sent your son to heal the sick, to feed the hungry, and to bring salvation to all people. Help me to follow in Jesus' footsteps, to love others as he loved us, and to bear good fruit in all that I do.
Thank you for this powerful reminder of your love and grace. May I always seek to live out that love in my life, and may my words and actions be a reflection of your mercy and compassion.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #8
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #8
Dear Lord,

As I read through Matthew chapter 8, I am reminded of your power and authority over all things. In this chapter, we see numerous examples of your healing power, your control over the elements, and your authority over even the demons themselves. It is a powerful reminder of your divinity and your love for us.

The chapter begins with the healing of a leper. In those times, lepers were shunned and cast out of society, but you had compassion on him and healed him. You are always willing to reach out and heal our deepest wounds, no matter how much we may feel unworthy or rejected.

Then we read about the healing of a centurion's servant, which shows us that your healing power knows no bounds. You don't require proximity or even physical contact to heal us. Your word alone is enough to heal and restore us.

In the next section, we see your power over the elements, as you calm the storm on the sea. Your disciples were fearful for their lives, but you were able to speak to the winds and waves and bring peace to the chaos. This reminds me that even when the storms of life are raging around me, you are always in control and can bring peace to my troubled heart.

Lastly, we see your authority over the demons, as you cast them out of two possessed men. The demons recognized you as the Son of God and begged to be sent into a herd of pigs instead. This shows us that even the forces of evil must submit to your authority, and we can have confidence that you are more powerful than any spiritual attack we may face.

Lord, thank you for your power and your love for us. Help me to remember these examples of your authority as I face the challenges and struggles of daily life. May I always trust in your power to heal, calm, and deliver me. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #20
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #20
Dear God,

As I read through Matthew chapter 20, I am struck by the theme of servanthood and humility that runs throughout the chapter. In this chapter, we see Jesus teaching his disciples about what it means to be a servant and how true greatness is found in serving others.

One of the most powerful examples of this is found in the parable of the workers in the vineyard. In this parable, we see a landowner who goes out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard. Throughout the day, he hires more workers, with the last ones being hired in the late afternoon. When it comes time to pay the workers, he pays them all the same amount, regardless of how long they worked. This causes the workers who were hired earlier in the day to complain, but the landowner responds by saying, "I am not being unfair to you, friend. Didn't you agree to work for a denarius? Take your pay and go. I want to give the one who was hired last the same as I gave you. Don't I have the right to do what I want with my own money? Or are you envious because I am generous?"

This parable reminds me that as a follower of Jesus, I am called to serve others, not for my own gain, but for the sake of the kingdom of God. I am called to be generous and to show love to others, regardless of how much they have done or how long they have been a part of the community of believers.

Lord, help me to have a servant's heart like Jesus. Help me to put the needs of others before my own and to be willing to serve wherever and whenever you call me. May I never become envious of others or focus on my own desires, but instead may I always seek to glorify you through my service to others.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #15
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #15
Dear God,

As I read Matthew chapter 15 today, I was struck by how the religious leaders of the time were so focused on the external practices of religion, while neglecting the true heart of it. Jesus rebuked them for their hypocrisy and reminded them that it's not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of it.

This reminds me of how easy it is to get caught up in the outward expressions of faith, without truly examining our hearts and motives. We can go through the motions of prayer, attending church, and reading the Bible, but if our hearts aren't in the right place, it's all for nothing.

Lord, I pray that you would help me to truly seek you with my whole heart, and not just go through the motions of religious practice. Help me to examine my heart and motives, and to repent of anything that is not pleasing to you.

I also want to take note of the faith of the Canaanite woman who came to Jesus pleading for her daughter's healing. Despite being told by the disciples to go away, and even being called a dog by Jesus himself, she persisted in her faith and humility. She recognized Jesus as the Son of David and begged for his mercy. And because of her faith, her daughter was healed.

Lord, I want to have the kind of faith that the Canaanite woman had. Help me to persist in my prayers and to trust in your mercy and grace, even when the answer seems delayed or the situation seems impossible. Help me to recognize you as the Son of God, and to trust in your power to heal and restore.
Thank you for your word, Lord, and for the lessons it teaches us about true faith and the condition of our hearts. May we always seek you with all our heart, soul, and mind.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #29
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #29
Dear God,

As I begin to read and reflect on Mark 1, I am struck by the urgency with which Jesus begins His ministry. We see Him baptised by John the Baptist and immediately led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by Satan. He then begins to preach and heal with an authority that astounds the people who witness His actions.

Lord, I am reminded that You call us to a life of action and service. Just as Jesus wasted no time in beginning His ministry, we are called to use our time and gifts to serve others and spread the good news of Your love and salvation. It can be easy to become complacent or distracted, but the urgency of Jesus' ministry serves as a reminder to always be focused on Your will and purpose for our lives.

As I continue to read, I am also struck by the humility and compassion Jesus demonstrates in His interactions with those around Him. He heals those who are sick and reaches out to those who are marginalized, showing them love and acceptance. Lord, help me to emulate this same love and compassion in my own life. Help me to be mindful of those around me who may be hurting or in need, and to show them Your love through my actions and words.

Finally, Lord, I am reminded of the importance of prayer and solitude in our lives. Jesus often withdrew to quiet places to pray and connect with You. In a world that is so busy and noisy, it can be easy to neglect this vital aspect of our relationship with You. Help me to prioritize my time with You, and to seek Your guidance and wisdom as I navigate the challenges and opportunities of each day.
Thank You, Lord, for the lessons and reminders found in Mark 1. May I continue to grow in my faith and service to You each day. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #7
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #7
Dear God,

Today I read Matthew chapter 7, and I am in awe of the wisdom and guidance you have provided in these verses. As I reflect on these words, I am reminded of the importance of putting my trust in you and following your teachings.

Verse 1 starts with a warning about judging others. It is a powerful reminder that I should not judge others, as I will be judged in the same way. It's easy to become critical of others, but I must remember that I am not perfect and have flaws of my own.

In verse 7, you encourage us to ask, seek, and knock. I am reminded of the power of prayer and how it can transform my life. I am grateful for the reminder to come to you in prayer, knowing that you are always there to listen and answer.

Verse 12 speaks of the golden rule, treating others as we would like to be treated. This is a timeless and universal principle that is so important in our interactions with others. Help me to live this principle in my daily life.

As I read further, I am reminded of the importance of choosing the right path in life. The narrow gate is the way to eternal life, but it is not always the easiest path. Help me to stay focused on you and to walk the narrow path, even when it is difficult.

Verse 24 reminds me that building my life on a solid foundation is essential. Only by building on your word and following your teachings can I ensure that my life is grounded in truth and will withstand the storms of life.

I am grateful for the insights and guidance found in Matthew chapter 7. Help me to apply these principles in my daily life, and to grow in faith and obedience to you. Thank you for your unending love and grace.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #28
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #28
Dear God,

Today I read Matthew chapter 28, and it has left me feeling incredibly inspired and uplifted. This chapter tells the story of your son, Jesus Christ, rising from the dead and ascending to heaven. It's a powerful reminder of your love and the incredible sacrifice Jesus made for us.

As I read through this chapter, I can't help but feel a sense of awe and wonder. Your power and love are truly amazing. Even death could not hold Jesus down, and through his resurrection, we are offered the gift of eternal life. It's a gift that I am so grateful for and one that I don't take lightly.

The chapter begins with the women coming to Jesus' tomb to anoint his body. However, when they arrive, they find the tomb empty, and an angel tells them that Jesus has risen. This is such an incredible moment and one that reminds me that you are always with us, even in the darkest moments.

Later in the chapter, Jesus appears to his disciples, and he gives them the Great Commission, telling them to go and make disciples of all nations. It's a powerful reminder that as your followers, we are called to share your love and grace with others. We are called to be your hands and feet in this world and to spread your message of hope.

As I reflect on this chapter, I am reminded that you are always with me. Even in the midst of challenges and struggles, I can find hope and strength in you. I am grateful for the sacrifice that Jesus made for me, and I am inspired to share your love with others.
Thank you for your incredible love and grace. May I always seek to follow you and to share your message with others.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #19
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #19
Dear God,
As I reflect on Matthew chapter 19, I am reminded of the importance of surrendering my life to You and trusting in Your plans.

In the beginning of the chapter, Jesus speaks about divorce and the sanctity of marriage. He reminds us that marriage is not to be taken lightly and that divorce should only be considered in extreme cases of infidelity. This teaches me the importance of valuing and cherishing the relationships You have blessed me with, and to work through any struggles that may arise.

Next, Jesus interacts with the rich young man who asks how he can attain eternal life. Despite the man's good intentions, Jesus shows him that he is still holding onto his wealth and that he needs to surrender everything to follow Him. This challenges me to examine my own heart and consider what things in my life I may be holding onto instead of fully trusting in You.

Later in the chapter, Jesus speaks about the difficulty of entering the kingdom of heaven, comparing it to a camel passing through the eye of a needle. This reminds me that salvation is not something I can earn or achieve on my own, but rather a gift from You that I must humbly accept.

Finally, Jesus assures His disciples that those who have given up everything to follow Him will be rewarded in the end. This gives me hope and encourages me to continue to surrender my life to You, even when it may be difficult or uncomfortable.

Lord, I pray that You would help me to trust in Your plans for my life and to surrender everything to You. May I value my relationships, seek Your will above my own desires, and trust in Your grace and mercy for my salvation. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #34
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #34
Dear God,

Today I read Mark 6 and was struck by the way Jesus interacted with the people around him. In this chapter, we see Jesus teaching in his hometown of Nazareth, sending out his disciples to preach and heal, feeding the 5,000, and walking on water.

As I read, I was reminded of how powerful and compassionate you are. You have the ability to heal the sick, feed the hungry, and calm the storms of life. You are not limited by our circumstances, and you can do far more than we could ever imagine.

But I was also struck by how the people around Jesus responded to him. In Nazareth, the people were skeptical of Jesus and did not believe in his power. They were so focused on their own perceptions of him that they missed out on the miracles he could have done for them.

On the other hand, the crowds who followed Jesus were eager to receive his teaching and healing. They recognized him as someone special and were willing to follow him wherever he went. Even when Jesus withdrew to a quiet place, they followed him there, hungry for more of his words and presence.

Lord, I pray that I would be like those who followed Jesus, eager to learn from him and be in his presence. Help me to recognize your power and trust in you, even when things seem impossible. And help me to avoid being like those in Nazareth, who doubted and missed out on your blessings.

Thank you for your endless grace and mercy, and for the many ways you show your love to us each day. May we never take your goodness for granted, but always seek to honor and serve you in all that we do.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #38
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #38
Dear God,

As I read through Mark 10 today, I am struck by the lessons that Jesus teaches about humility, sacrifice, and faith. The chapter begins with Jesus teaching the Pharisees about divorce, emphasizing the sanctity of marriage and the commitment that is required in a covenant relationship. He then goes on to bless the children, showing us the importance of childlike faith and humility.

As I reflect on these teachings, I am reminded of my own need to surrender my will and desires to you. Help me to trust in your plans and your timing, even when it is difficult or uncomfortable. Help me to be like a child, trusting and dependent on you for everything.

Later in the chapter, we see the story of the rich young man who asks Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal life. Jesus tells him to sell everything he has and follow him, but the young man cannot bring himself to do it. This story challenges me to examine my own priorities and attachments. What am I holding onto that is keeping me from fully following you? Help me to be willing to sacrifice whatever is necessary to obey your will.

Finally, we see the story of James and John, who ask Jesus to grant them positions of honor in his kingdom. Jesus responds by telling them that the greatest in his kingdom will be the servant of all. This reminds me that true greatness is found in serving others, not in seeking power or recognition for ourselves.
As I go about my day, help me to remember these lessons from Mark 10. Help me to have childlike faith, to be willing to sacrifice everything for you, and to seek greatness through serving others.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #33
paragraphs: Daily  Devotional #33
Dear God,

As I read Mark 5 today, I am struck by the many miracles that Jesus performed. The chapter starts with the story of the demon-possessed man, who was living among the tombs and was tormented by evil spirits. Jesus freed him from the demons, and the man was able to return to his family and community.

Next, we read about the healing of the woman with the issue of blood. She had been suffering for 12 years and had spent all her money on doctors, but none of them could heal her. However, when she touched Jesus' garment, she was immediately healed.

Finally, we read about the healing of Jairus' daughter. Jairus, a synagogue leader, begged Jesus to come and heal his daughter, who was dying. Despite the ridicule of the mourners who believed the girl was already dead, Jesus took her by the hand and brought her back to life.

Lord, as I reflect on these stories, I am reminded of your power and your compassion. You have the power to heal and to free us from the things that torment us. You care about our suffering and want to bring us back to life.

Help me to have faith like the demon-possessed man, who recognized Jesus' authority and begged to be healed. Help me to have faith like the woman with the issue of blood, who believed that just touching Jesus' garment would bring healing. Help me to have faith like Jairus, who trusted that Jesus could bring his daughter back to life.
Lord, I know that you are still in the business of performing miracles today. Help me to recognize your power and your presence in my life, and to trust you with all my heart.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #16
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #16
Dear God,

As I read through Matthew chapter 16, I am reminded of the importance of recognizing who You are and the significance of Your Son, Jesus Christ. In this chapter, Jesus asked His disciples who people thought He was, and they responded with various answers. But then Jesus asked them directly, "Who do you say I am?" Peter spoke up and said, "You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God."

I am struck by Peter's boldness and conviction in declaring who Jesus is. Lord, help me to have that same boldness and clarity in my own faith. Help me to always remember that You are the Messiah, the Savior of the world, and that there is no other way to salvation except through You.

I am also reminded of Jesus' promise to build His church, and how the gates of hell will not overcome it. This gives me great hope and encouragement, especially during times of uncertainty and difficulty. No matter what challenges may come, Your church will always prevail because You are in control.

As I continue to read through this chapter, I am confronted with Jesus' words about taking up our cross and following Him. This is a difficult truth to accept, but it is a necessary one. Help me to be willing to lay down my own desires and ambitions, and to follow You wholeheartedly, no matter the cost.

Lord, thank You for the gift of Your Son and for the promise of eternal life through Him. Help me to keep my eyes fixed on Him and to trust in Your plans for my life. May Your will be done, both in my life and in the world around me.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #36
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #36
Dear God,

As I read through Mark 8, I am reminded of the incredible miracles you performed during Jesus' time on earth. From feeding the four thousand to healing a blind man, your power and love are evident throughout this chapter.

One passage that particularly stands out to me is when Jesus asked his disciples, "Who do you say I am?" Peter answered, "You are the Messiah." This declaration of faith was not just a recognition of Jesus' identity, but also a declaration of trust and belief in him.

Lord, I too declare that you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God. I place my trust and belief in you, knowing that you are the one who can save me from my sins and guide me on the path of righteousness.

But, Lord, I also confess that my faith can be weak at times. Like the disciples who doubted when they were faced with the challenge of feeding the four thousand, I too can become overwhelmed by the challenges and struggles of life.

Help me to remember that with you, all things are possible. You can provide for me and sustain me even in the midst of difficulty. May I always trust in your goodness and faithfulness, even when I cannot see the way forward.

Lord, I pray that my faith in you will continue to grow stronger with each passing day. May I always remember that you are the Messiah, the one who has the power to save and redeem me. And may my life be a reflection of your love and grace to those around me.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #14
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #14
Dear God,

Today, as I read Matthew chapter 14, I am struck by the miracle of Jesus feeding the 5000. It's incredible to think about how You can take something as small as five loaves of bread and two fish and multiply it to feed such a large crowd. This is a powerful reminder of Your abundance and provision.

But there's more to this chapter than just the miracle of the loaves and fish. We also see Jesus walking on water, and Peter's attempt to do the same. I am reminded of the importance of faith and trust in You. Peter had faith that he could walk on water, but when he took his eyes off of You and began to focus on the wind and waves, he began to sink. It's a powerful lesson for me to remember to keep my focus on You, even when things around me seem chaotic.

And then there's the story of John the Baptist's death. It's a tragic event, but it's also a reminder of the cost of following You. John was willing to speak the truth and confront those in power, even if it meant his own life. It's a challenge for me to be bold and courageous in my own faith, even if it means facing opposition or persecution.

Overall, Matthew chapter 14 is a powerful reminder of Your provision, the importance of faith and trust, and the cost of following You. Help me to keep my focus on You, to trust in Your abundance, and to be bold and courageous in my faith.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #24
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #24
Dear God,

As I reflect on Matthew chapter 24, I am reminded of the importance of staying alert and prepared for Your return. Jesus warns us about false teachers who will come and deceive many. It is so easy to be misled by those who claim to have the truth but really lead us away from You.

Jesus also tells us about the signs that will precede His coming - wars, rumors of wars, famine, earthquakes, and other natural disasters. These are all indicators that the end is near, and we must be prepared to face them.

Lord, as I read these words, I can't help but feel a sense of urgency. It's easy to get caught up in the distractions of this world, but I know that my time here is temporary. Help me to keep my focus on You and to prioritize my relationship with You above all else.

I am comforted by Jesus' words that no one knows the day or hour of His return, not even the angels in heaven. It is not for me to worry about the exact timing, but rather to be ready for whenever it may happen.

Lord, I pray for the strength and wisdom to discern truth from deception and to remain steadfast in my faith even in the midst of trials and tribulations. May I always be found faithful and prepared when You return.
Thank You for Your love and grace, and for the assurance that You are with me always.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #23
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #23
Dear God,

As I read Matthew Chapter 23, I am struck by the words of Jesus as he rebukes the Pharisees and teachers of the law for their hypocrisy and pride. He warns his followers not to follow their example, for they may lead others astray.

It is a sobering reminder that being a leader, especially a spiritual leader, comes with great responsibility. It is not enough to simply teach your followers the right things to do, but you must also model it in your own life.

Lord, I pray for humility in my own life. May I not become prideful or hypocritical in my actions and words. May I always seek to serve others and point them towards you, rather than seeking my own glory or recognition.

I am also reminded of the importance of being a servant leader. Jesus himself came not to be served, but to serve and give his life as a ransom for many. May I follow his example and always seek to serve those around me, rather than expecting them to serve me.

Finally, I am reminded of the importance of obedience. Jesus tells the Pharisees that they have neglected the more important matters of the law- justice, mercy, and faithfulness. May I always prioritize these things in my own life and seek to obey your commands, rather than just going through the motions.
Thank you for this reminder today, Lord. May I continue to grow in humility, servanthood, and obedience as I follow you.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #35
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #35
Dear Father God,

Today, as I read through Mark 7, I am struck by Jesus' words that it is not what goes into a person that defiles them, but what comes out of their heart. As I reflect on this, I realize how often I focus on outward appearances and actions, rather than the state of my heart.

It's easy to fall into the trap of thinking that if I just do all the right things, then I am good enough. But Jesus reminds me that true worship and righteousness come from a pure heart, not just external actions.

As I examine my heart today, I realize that there are areas where I need to confess and seek forgiveness. I have been quick to judge others, thinking that my outward actions make me better than them. But Jesus calls me to examine the condition of my heart and to seek to remove any impurities within.
I am grateful that Jesus offers us a way to purify our hearts through his sacrifice on the cross. As I turn to him in repentance, I know that he will cleanse me and transform me from the inside out.

Lord, today I ask for your forgiveness for any impurities in my heart. I pray that you would help me to focus not just on external actions, but on the state of my heart. Help me to worship you in spirit and in truth, with a pure heart that reflects your love and grace. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #30
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #30
Dear God,

As I read through Mark 2 today, I am struck by the incredible faith of the paralyzed man's friends. They were determined to bring him to Jesus, no matter what it took. They believed that Jesus could heal their friend, and they were willing to do whatever it took to get him to Jesus.

As I reflect on this story, I am reminded of the importance of having a strong faith in you. These friends had such faith that they were willing to go to great lengths to bring their friend to you. They didn't let obstacles like a crowded house stop them from getting to you. They were persistent and determined, and because of their faith, their friend was healed.

Lord, help me to have that kind of faith. Help me to trust in you completely and to believe that you are able to do anything. When I face obstacles or challenges, help me to remember that nothing is impossible for you. Help me to be persistent and determined in my faith, just like the paralyzed man's friends.
Thank you for this powerful reminder of the importance of faith. I pray that I will continue to grow in my faith and trust in you more and more each day.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)
